rules.objective: The first partnership to reach nine points wins. Points are scored from tricks (one point per trick in excess of six) and from honours (AKQJ of trumps: two points for three honours, four points for all four).
rules.gameplay: Four players in two partnerships (partners opposite). Twelve cards each, dealt four at a time. Top card of the four-card stock determines trump. Holder of the Ace of trump (or dealer if Ace is exposed) ruffs by taking the stock and discarding four cards. Player to dealer's left leads; all follow suit if possible, otherwise may play any card. Trick is won by the highest trump, or if no trump played, by the highest card of the led suit. Twelve tricks per deal. Honours may be declared to end the game (except on eight points): declare three or more in hand, or with two call Can-ye for partner's honours.
keyRules: 17th-century English Whist ancestor; related to Ruff and Trump.
Follow suit if possible; trick won by highest trump or highest card of led suit.
One point per trick over six; honours (AKQJ of trumps) score two for three, four for all four.
First partnership to nine points wins.
